title: Go SDK response-transformer registry + resilient-stream connector with adaptive backoff
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Background:
We need a maintainable way to map raw streaming frames and final responses into typed Go structs while keeping ergonomics for consumers that use generics. Existing helpers are fragmented (many packages with ad-hoc decoders) and retry/backpressure semantics live in a different layer, which makes it hard to perform end-to-end integration tests and reason about failure modes.

Goals:
- Add a small registry (response-transformer factory) that maps model & route -> typed transformer functions (using Go 1.20+ generics).
- Provide a resilient-stream connector that wires the HTTP/WS stream, applies transformers to frames (partial + final), and exposes a unified consumer API that supports: context cancellation, structured decode errors, and automatic adaptive retry/backoff for idempotent requests.
- Ensure the API is lightweight for common use (one-liners for prompts->typed-response) and extensible for advanced usage (custom transformers, partial frame hooks).
- Integrate with existing metrics/tracing (console and runtime) and surface transformation errors in Console rollups.

Acceptance criteria:
1) New transformer registry with tests for: JSON decode, partial-chunk aggregation, and schema mismatch handling.
2) ResilientStreamConnector provides: Stream (chan Event[T]), Close() error, and RetryPolicy hook.
3) Demonstration app converting streaming chat responses into typed ChatMessage structs with a README example.
4) Performance: added latency <= +1ms p50 for typical 32-token responses when connector is enabled.
5) Integration tests that exercise the adaptive retry path using recorded HTTP failures.

Design notes / API sketch:
- Transformer definition (example):

  type Transformer[T any] func(frame []byte, isFinal bool) (T, error)

- Registry: simple map keyed by model+route with Register/Lookup. Keep implementation interface small so customers can override for specific models.

- ResilientStreamConnector responsibilities:
  - Establish the streaming connection (http/2 or websocket).
  - Perform backpressure-aware reads and forward frames to transformer.
  - Manage a per-request retry policy: for idempotent requests allow N retries with exponential jitter; for non-idempotent only do transparent reconnects that do not duplicate client-visible responses.
  - Emit events on failure for Console to capture (transformation_error, retry_attempt, final_response).

- Retry policy: adaptive based on observed server-side error rates and client-side latency. Default: {maxRetries:3, baseDelay:100ms, maxDelay:2s} with jitter. Expose hooks for custom policy.

Trade-offs considered:
- Central registry vs explicit transformer injection: registry simplifies quickstarts but adds global state. We chose a registry with explicit override on request options to balance both.
- Generic transformer vs interface-based: generics produce nicer APIs for callers but require Go 1.18+. We will document min supported Go version and provide small adapter for non-generic callers.

Migration / rollout plan:
1) Implement registry + connector in a new internal package: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/streamx.
2) Add unit tests & integration harness that replays recorded streams.
3) Feature-flag the resilient connector behind an opt-in SDK option; keep current streaming codepath as default.
4) Gradual rollout: internal dogfood -> opt-in beta customers -> default in go-sdk-0.10.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for registry lookup and transformer error propagation.
- Integration tests using a small HTTP mock server that sends partial frames and closes mid-stream. Verify connector retry behavior.
- Load test for latency/regression (compare baseline p50/p95 before & after).

Observability:
- Emit tracing spans: stream.connect, stream.transform, stream.retry.
- Counters: transform_errors_total, transform_success_total, retry_attempts_total.
- Add Console dashboard tiles for these metrics and add a sample Trace view in the PR.

Docs / Examples:
- README in streamx/ with: simple_chat_example.go showing typed ChatMessage usage, partial frame handling example, and custom transformer registration.
- Migration guide for customers using older ad-hoc decoders.

Security / Privacy:
- Transformers run in-process; ensure we never log raw user tokens or prompt text in production sampling. Mark transformation_error traces as safe for logs (avoid PII).

Open questions:
- Should registry be per-Client instance instead of global? (TBD — leaning toward per-Client with a global default to reduce surprising mutations.)
- Exact backoff tuning for low-latency flows; will iterate based on dogfood metrics.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Triage: scoped down to MVP: registry + connector + basic retry. Priya assigned. Estimated 5 points.
2025-02-18 - Design review: UX ok. Design asked to prefer per-Client registry defaulting to global. Diego to update API sketch.
2025-02-24 - Implementation: initial package scaffolded (streamx). Added Transformer type + registry. See branch: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/873
2025-02-26 - Code review: @Elliot suggested exposing a streaming iterator helper (Next() (T, error)) to make for-loops ergonomic; added as opt-in helper.
2025-03-01 - Integration tests added for retry scenarios. Found an edge-case: transformer returning schema mismatch should fail the request (no retry) — updated logic accordingly.
2025-03-03 - QA: Load test shows p95 increase ~1.7ms on small messages—within acceptable threshold. Preparing PR for merge and feature-flag rollout.
